name: wolf
about: Chain ragdoll body for the wolf (31-bone quadruped rig, identical skeleton to the elephant's). 13 capsules: hips (root, spine0), chest, head (with neck), tail_a, tail_b, and 4 legs x (upper, lower). Bones without a body (spine1, spine3, spine4, ears, jaw, pasterns, paws, tail1, tail3) follow their parent bone in the scene graph. A lighter, long-legged quadruped: slim torso, thin limbs, wide leg swing and a deep knee fold. Every number is here; src/chain.mjs holds none.
placeholder_note: radii, masses, joint limits and motor scales are PLACEHOLDERS to tune on Dom's phone and the clips; only the bone positions are measured.
scale_source: Armagedom Web/src/data/creatureDefinitions.json original-wolf scale.model 2.5: bones and radii below are in model units, the row is in metres at this scale (about 2.4 m long, 1.2 m at the ear tip)
mass_assumption: placeholder: a real wolf is about 40 kg and 1.5 m long; this one is about 2.4 m long, so about 4x the volume, call it 140 kg. The game data gives hp 40 and no mass.
inertia_source: data/ragdoll-role-table.json motor.inertia_multiplier (M1 finding), same value as the humanoid rows
hinge_flex_z_source: own: the creature faces +z. A hind hock flexes the lower leg backward (-z); a front elbow flexes it forward (+z). Same convention as the salamander.
